text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentThe World’s Largest Marine Turtle Makes a Move SouthNesting leatherbacks chase cooler waters to Ecuador’s beachesDRBy Devin Reese5:00 PM CST on November 13, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleLeatherbacks aren’t only spectacular for bodies that rival grand pianos in size and weight, but also for their temperature tolerances. By taking refuge in cool upwellings, they can inhabit tropical waters up to 86°F; on the flip side, by warming their bodies with activity and insulating fat, they can tolerate waters as cold as 32°F. But even leatherbacks have their limits. Powered By 1067.5K 2ShareNextStayA recent study in the journal Chelonian Conservation and Biology found that warming oceans are shifting the nesting sites of leatherback sea turtles (Dermochelys coriacea) to cooler waters. Typically, the critically endangered population of eastern Pacific leatherbacks concentrates its nesting along the west coasts of Mexico and Costa Rica. Now, though, they’re showing up about 1,000 miles south in Ecuador. Read more: “How Sea Turtles Find Their Way”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
